_note: US -> UK spellings. `en.json` is written in US English -- BMW's descriptor
paths are US (`...wheel.left.tire.pressure`), so the entity IDs users type
are `tire_*`, and the names should match them. `en-GB.json` is generated
from this map as a *delta*: Home Assistant loads `en` first and overlays the
requested language on top of it key by key, so only the strings that
actually differ need to exist. The card's `t()` falls back the same way.
Applied case-preserving and whole-word only, so `Tire`/`tire`/`TIRE` all
convert and `tire_status` (a translation key, never a display string) does
not. Values only -- keys are slugs and must never move.
Inflections are listed individually rather than stemmed: a word list that
cannot be clever also cannot be wrong.

Lists the cluster slugs the user types -- `electric, status, tire` -- not words. `tyre` is not a slug we accept, so translating this string would hand a British user a value that silently matches nothing.

_deliberately_absent.meter: The four `meter`s in en.json are all the device -- a wallbox, house or grid meter -- which is spelled the same in both dialects. Only the unit of length is `metre`, so a blind `meter` -> `metre` would mangle every one of them. `kilometer` below is unambiguous and is mapped.
_deliberately_absent.license: `licence` is the UK *noun* only; the verb stays `license` in both dialects. Not worth the risk for a word that does not occur.
_deliberately_absent.catalog: We write `catalogue` everywhere already -- it is BMW's own term for the descriptor export and is accepted in US English. Mapping it would make the guard test flag our own vocabulary as British.
_deliberately_absent.program: A computer program is `program` in both dialects; only the unrelated sense (a TV programme) differs.
